verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce documents a public REST API. Enrollment is POST /acp/v1/tokens, purchase intents are POST /acp/v1/instructions (with cancellation), and credentials are retrieved via POST /acp/v1/instructions/{instructionID}/credentials, all with production and test base URLs and a self-serve sandbox for test transactions. A probe confirms the Visa developer gateway is live and credential-gated as documented. Missing for 10: hands-on corroboration of calls to the /acp endpoints themselves (the probe only hit a helloworld gateway), and production maturity, since docs say the product is "in the process of development and deployment" and production access requires contacting Visa.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Your agents can enroll a customer's card for tokenization during the customer's account registration or when the customer begins a new purchase intent
Your agent can cancel a purchase intent when the customer chooses to not make the purchase.
After completing the evaluation registration process, you will be able to send test transactions
Developers can now connect to Visa Intelligent Commerce APIs through the MCP Server, making it faster and easier for builders to bring intelligent, payment-enabled experiences to life.
